digest.component_or_area: Jira Reconciler – baseline advance and inbound arbitration
propositions: Operator local status changes are silently reverted by the reconciler when the change reverts to a pre-push baseline value within one pass after rebar's own outbound push, because the baseline is advanced from the pre-push snapshot rather than the post-push synced state.

The guard _suppressed_by_inbound fires incorrectly when local == stale baseline (pre-push value), causing outbound to omit the field and inbound to clobber with Jira's current value, while other fields from the same window survive because they differ from the baseline.

The baseline must be advanced to the last-SYNCED value (what rebar actually pushed) rather than last-FETCHED (pre-push snapshot), gated on per-mutation success to avoid recording syncs that soft-failed and did not land.

The defect affects all five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) because they all share the _suppressed_by_inbound guard and therefore all share the ABA exposure.

ADR 0026's mandated direction-preservation regression cell exists only for title; status and other mirrored fields lack live-path coverage (tests drive the dead-code path _diff_fields instead of the production diff_canonical_fields), allowing the baseline defect to go undetected.
